description: Conformance table for fragment op appliers: the host-side code that turns a finalized command buffer into DOM. Each case is plain data, `(dom, ops) -> (expected.dom, expected.writes)`, and names in `because` the applier defect it exists to catch. The runtime's op corpus (`fragment-op-tests.json`) holds the runtime to what it emits; this table holds a host to what it does with it.
notes: `dom` and `expected.dom` are the children of a container element, written as J5ML: `[name, {attributes}?, ...children]`, a string being a text node.

`ops` are finalized ops exactly as a host receives them from `fireFragmentHook`, including the parsed `target`. A few cases carry an op shape the runtime no longer emits (`setAttr` with `false` or `null`), because an applier also meets op lists a host assembled itself or received from an older runtime.

Snapshots compare after normalization: attributes are compared as a set, the `class` attribute as a set of tokens with an empty `class` the same as an absent one, the `hidden` attribute by presence alone, and adjacent text nodes merged with empty ones dropped.

A write is a mutating call on the DOM: setting an attribute, removing an attribute that is present, adding or removing a class, setting text content, or replacing children. Setting an attribute to the value it already holds is a write, and so is adding a class already present or removing one already absent, because a DOM still runs its update steps for those; removing an attribute that is absent is not. An applier stays at the expected count by reading before it writes. `expected.writes` is the exact count: an applier that writes more re-runs observers, transitions, and input state for nothing, and one that writes less skipped real work.

`toggle` is a set, not a flip. `value` is the strict boolean condition; `true` shows the target (no `hidden` attribute) and `false` hides it (`hidden` present). Toggle cases repeat an even number of times, because an applier that flips on every op lands on the right state after an odd number of repeats and on the wrong one after an even number.
`replaceChildren` carries a markup string, a list of markup strings (concatenated in order), or a J5ML node list. The empty list is an explicit clear.
Every op name in the vocabulary has at least one case: `toggle`, `setText`, `replaceChildren`, `setProp`, `setAttr`, `removeAttr`, `addClass`, `removeClass`.

cases.description: setAttr writes the attribute
cases.because: an applier that ignores setAttr, or reads only the deprecated `attr` key, drops the write

cases.description: setAttr repeated with the same value writes once
cases.because: an applier that re-writes identical values fires a mutation for every repeat

cases.description: setAttr to the value already present does not write
cases.because: an applier that never compares against the current value re-writes state the fragment already has

cases.description: setAttr stringifies a number
cases.because: an applier that writes only string values drops numeric attributes

cases.description: setAttr false does not leave a present attribute
cases.because: an applier that stringifies every value writes disabled="false", which HTML reads as disabled

cases.description: setAttr null removes the attribute
cases.because: an applier that stringifies null writes the literal text "null"

cases.description: setAttr true writes the string true
cases.because: an applier that treats true as a removal, or writes an empty value, loses a string-boolean attribute such as aria-pressed

cases.description: removeAttr removes a present attribute
cases.because: an applier that does not know removeAttr has no way to undo a setAttr

cases.description: removeAttr on an absent attribute does not write
cases.because: removing what is not there is not a change

cases.description: setAttr then removeAttr applies in list order
cases.because: an applier that batches or reorders ops lands on the wrong final state

cases.description: setProp on an HTML node writes the attribute
cases.because: an applier that handles only the deprecated setAttr drops the canonical op

cases.description: setProp repeated with the same value writes once
cases.because: an applier that re-writes identical values fires a mutation for every repeat

cases.description: toggle false repeated twice hides
cases.because: an applier that flips visibility on each op ends visible after an even number of repeats

cases.description: toggle true repeated twice on a hidden node shows it
cases.because: an applier that flips visibility on each op ends hidden after an even number of repeats

cases.description: toggle true repeated four times on a visible node does not write
cases.because: a flipping applier toggles four times and an unconditional one writes four times; the set is already true

cases.description: toggle false then true then false then true lands on the last condition
cases.because: an applier that reads anything but the op's value drifts from the condition the mod set

cases.description: addClass adds an absent class
cases.because: an applier that replaces the class attribute instead of adding a token drops the classes already there

cases.description: addClass on a class already present does not write
cases.because: an applier that adds without checking re-writes the class attribute

cases.description: removeClass removes a present class and skips an absent one
cases.because: an applier that removes without checking re-writes the class attribute

cases.description: a selector target applies to every match
cases.because: an applier that resolves only the first match leaves the rest stale

cases.description: setText writes markup as literal text
cases.because: an applier that assigns innerHTML turns mod text into markup

cases.description: setText to the text already present does not write
cases.because: an applier that never compares re-writes text and resets selection inside it

cases.description: replaceChildren with a markup string replaces the children
cases.because: an applier that writes markup as text shows tags instead of nodes

cases.description: replaceChildren with a list of markup strings concatenates them in order
cases.because: an applier that expects a single string stringifies the list with commas between the items

cases.description: replaceChildren with an empty list clears
cases.because: an applier that skips an empty value as nothing-to-do leaves the old children in place

cases.description: replaceChildren with an empty string clears
cases.because: an applier that skips a falsy value leaves the old children in place

cases.description: replaceChildren with a J5ML node list builds the nodes
cases.because: an applier that stringifies a node list writes its JSON, or its comma-joined parts, as text

cases.description: an unresolvable target is a no-op
cases.because: an applier that throws on a missing node abandons the rest of the batch

cases.description: an unknown op name is ignored and the batch continues
cases.because: an applier that throws on an op a newer runtime emits abandons the ops after it

cases.description: setAttr with the string "false" writes the word
cases.because: an applier that reads the string "false" as a boolean removes an attribute like aria-expanded that needs the literal word

cases.description: toggle with no value changes nothing
cases.because: an applier that treats a missing condition as a flip brings flipping back for host-built op lists that omit the value

cases.description: setAttr on an event-handler attribute is refused
cases.because: an applier is the last floor for op lists a host assembled itself, and writing an on* attribute turns data into script

cases.description: setAttr with no value key removes the attribute
cases.because: a missing value means absent, and an applier that writes the string "undefined" leaves a present attribute
